passages.provision_quote: Notwithstanding section 15-2401, beginning in the 2022-2023 school year, in this chapter, unless the context otherwise requires, "qualified student" includes a resident of this state who both: 1. Is eligible to enroll in a public school in this state in any of the following: ( a ) A preschool program for children with disabilities. ( b ) A kindergarten program. ( c ) Any of grades one through twelve. 2. Does not otherwise qualify for an Arizona empowerment scholarship account pursuant to this chapter.
passages.note: Chaptered text of the version voted on; section 2 makes every student eligible to enroll in an Arizona public school a qualified student, and 15-2402 sends the per-pupil money to the parent-directed account.
House Third Reading roll call: Diaz voted Y, and the 31-26 split is well short of near-unanimous.
passages.actor_quote: DEGRAZIA N DIAZ Y DUNN Y

passages.note: Bill overview page listing Diaz as a co-sponsor of HB2853 and the governor's signature as Chapter 388.

rows.reasoning: HB2853 (2022) added section 15-2401.01, making any resident "eligible to enroll in a public school in this state" in "Any of grades one through twelve" a qualified student, and 15-2402 transfers "an amount that is equivalent to ninety percent of the sum of the base support level and additional assistance" into a parent-directed account spendable on "Tuition or fees at a qualified school" (any nongovernmental school, with no religious exclusion) or on "Services provided by a public school". Diaz co-sponsored this single-subject ESA bill and voted Y at House Third Reading (31-26-3-0-0), within his 2021-2023 term in the same chamber. That enacts universal eligibility so that "education funding follows the student to any school" chosen by the family, not eligibility for "most families".
